title: Proof built in
summary: Auditors want proof: who did what, who can see what, and that data is protected.

steps.title: Prove it, do not promise it
steps.text: Handling health, money or personal data comes with rules. An audit asks for evidence, not promises: a log nobody can edit, encryption with managed keys, one controlled place for personal data, tested backups, and a sign-in for every action.

steps.prompt: An audit lands at noon. Add what the auditors will ask for.
steps.hint: Place Audit log, Key management, Identity provider and Backups, then connect them to the servers and the database.

steps.title: Least privilege
steps.text: Give each person and each service only the access it needs, and record every use of it. Keep secrets out of code, and rotate keys. Most breaches come from a leaked key or an over-powered account, not from clever hacking.

rows.label: Test a backup restore
rows.how: an untested backup is a hope, approx.

steps.q: What does an auditor ask for?
choices: Promises that you will do better soon
A discount on the next audit
A tour of the whole office
Evidence you did what you said
In a pinned team chat message
Every team member gets admin rights
Access is shared by the whole team
Nobody can ever log in at all
Only the access a job needs

takeaway: Build the proof in from the start; adding it after the audit is far harder.
